steps.content: [Hilda's Room]
With Johnson's interrogation complete, the poisoning incident has reached a temporary resolution.
Once the room is cleared of the toxic source, Hilda offers you another fresh cup of black tea.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ${PlayerName}, do you also find my... interrogation methods unsettling?
She noticed how you'd unconsciously averted your gaze earlier, and it clearly troubled her. Now, she seizes the opportunity to ask.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I understand the necessity of forceful measures. Different subjects require different approaches. Since gentler methods were ineffective on Johnson, you simply escalated to what was "effective" on him.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I just wonder if there might have been another way... if it was truly necessary to go that far.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...I see. I was indeed too aggressive. I will exercise more restraint next time.
Her blunt confession throws you completely off balance. Flustered, you grab your teacup and take a hasty, unthinking gulp, only to be jolted by a scalding mouthful of tea.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Hot, hot, hot...!

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Take your time. Freshly brewed tea needs a moment to cool.
A hand appears, dabbing a handkerchief at the spilled tea before you.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...I should thank you. If not for your sharp eye catching the poison in that briefcase, the consequences would have been unthinkable.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No need for formalities. We all serve the same city-state. We all want to see the Monolith completed, to help us win this war.
You continue playing the role of the loyal metropole interrogator, following her conversational lead.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It's a shame that after all the commotion today, not a single one of them turned out to be the mole we're after.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: An experienced mole naturally prefers to hide behind its pawns, letting them take the risks. That's what makes it so difficult to catch.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: But... there's no need to rush. The Monolith's development is progressing smoothly. We still have time to catch that mole by the tail.
Setting her teacup down with a soft clink, she produces the secret letter found in Johnson's room. She then unfolds it and holds it over the veil of steam rising from the tea.
Before your eyes, the heat coaxes a secret from the paper: lines of invisible ink resolve into rows upon rows of densely packed numbers.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: As expected, the one pulling his strings was the mole. It knew exactly how to manipulate Johnson, offering him precisely what he desired most...

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: From Edward to Johnson, it's clear the "mole" isn't working alone. It was already recruiting allies from the moment it entered the manor.
She puts away the documents and looks at you with grave seriousness.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ${PlayerName}... if the mole ever attempts to compromise you, let me know immediately.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Maybe by then, I'll have already captured it myself and delivered it to you, all tied up.
Your remark earns a laugh from her, and it seems genuinely heartfelt.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Then, let's wish ourselves success in all our endeavors.

She tucks a stray strand of silver hair behind her ear, the usual tension in her expression melting away. It's a rare and unguarded softness. Seeing an opening in her good mood, you venture a subtle question.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: By the way, how did you crack that encrypted letter? Wasn't it just a bunch of numbers?

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: This type of cipher typically uses a specific book as its key. I simply happened to have memorized the correct one.
Without a flicker of emotion, she rises and pulls a small green booklet from the shelf, passing it to you. The utter lack of hesitation makes it clear: this is not the key used on the strip.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: The Wilderness. Each number corresponds to a page and a word's sequence on that page.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: The first word is in the "Readers' Letters" section.
After several fruitless passes through the pages, you can't locate the section she described. Instead, your search only yields "Midnight Tales" and "Musings and Reflections."

Puzzled, you turn to the front of the book, your finger gliding down the table of contents. It finally stops on a single, inconspicuous entry. As you start to turn to the corresponding page, a finger presses down on the book, stopping you cold.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: ...You've never read it before?
Her tone remains casual, but her gaze locks onto yours with the same unblinking intensity as the interrogation lamp that blazed down on Johnson.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: When it was popular in the metropoles, nearly every student had a copy.
It's a tactical error. Your instinctive flick through the pages the moment it touched your hands betrays you; the chance you'd be familiar with this decades-old popular poetry is zero.
Now, your mind scrambles, desperately reviewing the fragmented text you just glimpsed. Suddenly, one critical detail emerges from the chaos.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You're testing me?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I haven't read this particular edition. After so many years and reprints, the version I remember didn't have such a flashy binding.
With a calculated ease, Hilda releases her hold and withdraws her hand.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: If your memory is unclear, why not take this copy? Flip through it and give those verses a revisit. It may prove useful in the future.

With a nod of understanding, you carefully slide the book into your pocket. The shift in weight draws Hilda's attention; her eyes flicker over your attire, a calculated search for the cipher strip you took.
Too bad for her. You separated them the moment you had the chance. The strip is now safely hidden elsewhere; it will never find its way back into her possession.
Her expression betrays nothing. She simply looks away, rises, and crosses to the desk for paper and pen.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Officer ${PlayerName}, I'm grateful for everything you've done. However, your credentials remain unverified through official channels. This necessitates a degree of caution, despite my personal desire for a closer collaboration.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Therefore, I will be dispatching a formal inquiry to the city-state to confirm your identity. Should the verification be positive, you will receive a formal apology from me.

You nearly forgot—this estate is no sealed bubble, at least not for Hilda. She, as the owner, must have a line to the outside world. Your fabricated identity hangs by a thread, ready to snap at any moment.
After all, "you" are a ghost in the official records. The metropoles' officials could never have credentialed someone who doesn't exist.

The only saving grace is the Mania-charged air that clings to the estate, stifling electronic signals and slowing communication. To send a clear message, a guard would have to physically run it to a point beyond the grounds. It's a fragile delay, but it buys you precious time.
Your teacup is nearly empty. You drain the last bitter sip, the dregs catching in your throat like an omen.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I understand completely. If this resolves your concerns, it's for the best.

steps.speaker: Hilda
steps.content: Very well.
Hilda returns to the desk, draws a fresh sheet of letter paper, and begins to write, without even consulting her cipher book.
A gust of wind sweeps the corridor, causing the lamp flame to shudder. The only sound is the faint scratching of her pen, a rhythm that pulses in time with your own uneasy heartbeat.
Outside, the night deepens. The day's gentle drizzle swells into a torrent, lashing against the windows as if to wash the world clean.
[Main Hall]
In the main hall, Marlo fidgets with his lighter, the flame illuminating his gloomy face. He smokes restlessly, one after another, the glowing embers tracing his descent into deeper agitation.
[Room 2]
Filled with a quiet contentment after writing to her lover, Helene turns in for an early night.
[Underground Tunnel]
Under the cover of dim light, Manphist feels his way through the wine cellar. After carefully choosing two vintage bottles, he stealthily retreats to the sanctuary of his room.
[Corridor]
In the hallway, he runs into Huck. The man's face is clouded with a deep gloom. They acknowledge each other with only the barest of nods before continuing on their separate ways without a word.
[Room]
Nolaine spreads the day's gathered intelligence across the table, her eyes scanning the scattered pieces as she searches for a hidden thread connecting them.
[Corridor]
Johnson was summoned away abruptly and has never returned... leaving Casey to pace the corridor, each step wearing the floorboards thinner with her anxiety.
And so, the first night finally comes to an end.
